statement: (i) Write $f(x)=2\sin(x+\frac{\pi}{6})+\cos x$ as a single sine-plus-cosine combination and find its greatest value. (ii) Solve $2\sin(x+\frac{\pi}{6})=1$ for $0\le x\le 2\pi$. (iii) State the maximum of $f(x)$.
solution: (i) $2\sin(x+\frac{\pi}{6})=2(\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{6}+\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6})=\sqrt{3}\sin x+\cos x$, so $f(x)=\sqrt{3}\sin x+2\cos x$. Its greatest value is $\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{7}$. (ii) $\sin(x+\frac{\pi}{6})=\frac12\Rightarrow x+\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{13\pi}{6}$ (within range), giving $x=0,\frac{2\pi}{3},2\pi$. (iii) Maximum of $f$ is $\sqrt{7}$.
hints: Use the R-method for the maximum.
